professional_experience.description: The 2024 annual report lists Maxim Melnikov as chair of this board committee.

Cian/SEC annual report states he served as CEO since February 2014; official Cian release states he served in this capacity since 2014 and transferred responsibilities to Dmitriy Grigoriev effective 30 May 2022. Quality-pass note (2026-07-29): several Russian-language sources (Kommersant, rb.ru, ru.wikipedia.org, and Cian's own 2021 'top-20 leaders' retrospective) describe him becoming general director/managing partner in 2013 instead, an apparent conflict flagged in round 1. Additional research this round found a precise reconciliation via Forbes.ru: Media3's subsidiary Delovoy Mir Onlayn acquired Cian in July 2013, and leadership passed from Sergey Osipov to Melnikov roughly six months later (~early 2014) -- consistent with the SEC-filed February 2014 date. The 2013 references most likely describe the acquisition/his arrival at the group rather than the formal CEO title date. The SEC-filed 2014 date is kept as the more authoritative, legally-disclosed value for this entry; 2013 remains documented here as the resolved-but-not-adopted alternative rather than silently dropped.

Cian/SEC and HeadHunter SEC filings state that he served as CEO and director of Media3 Holding from 2010 to 2014. Quality-pass round 1 (2026-07-29) found this employer's own business described only by lower-tier aggregator sources and left sector/industry_group/industry null as a reasoned gap. QUALITY PASS ROUND 2 (2026-07-30): the HTML-readable text of Cian PLC's own SEC F-1 registration statement (filed 13 October 2021) and its 20-F for fiscal year 2022 (filed 27 April 2023 -- the first annual filing to also cover Grigoriev as CEO) were fetched directly (earlier rounds could only reach the cloudfront-hosted PDF rendering of this filing family and could not extract text from it). Both state, verbatim: 'From 2010 to 2014, Mr. Melnikov served as Chief Executive Officer and director for Media3 Holding, a large print and digital media holding company focused on selling print media businesses and investing in online media ventures.' This primary-source description was independently corroborated by ru.wikipedia.org's article on ЗАО «Медиа3» (verified directly, not only via a summarizing tool), which names Maxim Melnikov himself as its General Director and describes the group as owning Russia's largest printing facility (Krasnogorsk), a roughly 2,600-point retail print-distribution network across 14 regions, and the newspapers Труд, Экстра-М and Аргументы и факты (all sold or closed by August 2014, coinciding with the end of Melnikov's tenure and the Cian transition), alongside a number of internet portals; Wikipedia's own infobox classifies the company's industry as 'Медиа' (Media). Because both the primary SEC-filed description and the independent tertiary corroboration characterize Media3 Holding first and foremost as a diversified print/broadcast media conglomerate (not a pure-play online/interactive platform), sector/industry_group/industry are now filled in as Communication Services / Media & Entertainment / Media -- the exact gics_taxonomy.json row for traditional publishing/print media holding companies, distinct from the Interactive Media & Services row used for Cian itself and for Media3's own online-classifieds subsidiary. This replaces the prior round's informed null with a sourced, confirmed value; the previous null is documented here as superseded, not silently discarded.
Cian/SEC and HeadHunter 20-F sources state that he served on the board of HeadHunter Group PLC since May 2019.

validation_notes:
Processed 2 people for ticker CIAN. Checked 2 local documents in MOEXBMI_Отчеты_2024/CIAN before web search: the 2024 annual report and the 2024 IFRS consolidated financial statements. Total research rounds: 2 person-rounds (one round per person). Education was confirmed for both people; no confirmed research experience, publications, patents or h-index were found for either person. Weak/background sources were used only for context: RB.ru for Melnikov's 2013 leadership context and TAdviser as secondary confirmation for Grigoriev; core facts rely on local annual report, Cian official release, Cian/SEC filing, HeadHunter SEC filing, Cian interviews and Kommersant. Excluded namesakes include academic Dmitry/Dmitriy Grigoriev profiles in psychology, mathematics, paleontology and materials science; a vocalist Dmitry Grigoriev; Cumberland University professor Max Melnikov; hockey player Maxim Melnikov born 1999; and unrelated ORCID/Scholar Melnikov/Melnik profiles. Remaining gaps: exact FL.ru end year and Melnikov's specific pre-Media3 employers were not confirmed with enough precision. Search is considered complete because local documents were checked, official biographies were found, previous employers and education leads were followed, LinkedIn/snippet-only facts were not used without confirmation, and two expanded Russian/English search passes produced no unresolved high-quality leads.

ROUND 2 (2026-07-18, gap-filling per REFINEMENT.md, both people already fully identified in round 1 -- this round only fills previously null/vague fields and adds new required fields, it does not redo round-1 identity/career research):

1) Local documents re-checked first: MOEXBMI_Отчеты_2024/CIAN/МКПАО ЦИАН_Годовой отчет_2024_.pdf, pages 1-8, re-read specifically for the company's own business-model description (needed for the new GICS requirement, not previously extracted in round 1 which only covered the governance pages 55-58). No new personal-biography detail for either person was found there; this was expected and is not itself a gap.

2) sector/industry_group/industry added at company level: Communication Services / Media & Entertainment / Interactive Media & Services. Source: the company's own description in the local 2024 annual report and the official Cian press release. This matches gics_taxonomy.json exactly. Same triple applied to every professional_experience entry whose organization is Cian / MKPAO Cian in any of its legal-name variants, for both Grigoriev and Melnikov.

3) sector/industry_group/industry added to non-Cian professional_experience entries by the organization's own primary business: FL.ru (Grigoriev, CTO) = Industrials / Commercial & Professional Services / Professional Services. HeadHunter Group PLC (Melnikov, board member) = Industrials / Commercial & Professional Services / Professional Services. Two entries left null with justification: Choister; Rubrain (single entry combining two organizations with different primary businesses) and Media3 Holding (no source in round 1/2 described its business).

4) qualification_degree added to every education[]/degrees[] entry for both people. Grigoriev's MIET entry mapped to Specialist degree as a contextual inference from the specialty code/era (documented in research_notes). Melnikov's two entries mapped directly from explicit credential titles (Master's degree, MBA).

5) Institution normalization: Grigoriev's MIET string, Melnikov's Finance Academy string and Stanford GSB string normalized to their canonical university_names.json keys.

6) Remaining gaps re-attempted and confirmed to remain genuinely unresolved: Grigoriev's exact FL.ru end year; Melnikov's exact graduation years for both credentials; Melnikov's specific pre-Media3 employers.

7) No previously confirmed fact was deleted or overwritten. A backup of the pre-round-2 file was kept at output/CIAN_person_info.json.bak_before_round2.

ROUND 3/4 (2026-07-19): verification-only passes. All fields programmatically re-checked against gics_taxonomy.json / university_names.json / the qualification_degree enum; no discrepancy found. The remaining open gaps (FL.ru end year; Melnikov's education years and pre-Media3 employers) were each re-attempted via an independent tool path and confirmed to remain genuinely unresolved, not merely unexamined. Round 3's work had been researched but its sync into this validation_notes field and each person's notes field had not happened until round 4.

QUALITY PASS ROUND 1 (2026-07-29, see research_notes/CIAN/quality_pass_round1_20260729.md for full detail):

1) DESYNC FOUND AND FIXED (simple omission): the 2026-07-28 bulk QA-restore pass documented in QA_RECHECK_FIRST20_20260728.md (which restored clean Cyrillic from the backup_before_refinement_20260717_233715 snapshot and re-applied confirmed GICS / qualification_degree on top) had silently reverted this ticker to a pre-round-2 state for institution-name normalization and dropped two source citations, without touching the GICS / qualification_degree values themselves. Restored: Grigoriev's MIET institution string to its canonical university_names.json form; both of Melnikov's institution strings (Finance Academy, Stanford GSB) to their canonical forms in education[] and degrees[]; the fl.ru/about source (ceo and top-level); the ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/HeadHunter source (tmt[0] and top-level). Each person's notes field and this validation_notes field had also reverted to their round-1-only text, losing the round 2-4 documentation trail; that trail is restored above and this new section appended.

2) GENUINE INCONSISTENCY investigated and resolved: round 1 had flagged, but no subsequent round had actually re-investigated, a 2013-vs-2014 conflict for when Melnikov became Cian's CEO (SEC/Cian PLC 20-F and the official Cian press release say February 2014; Kommersant, rb.ru, ru.wikipedia.org and Cian's own 2021 top-20-leaders retrospective say 2013). Fresh research this round (Forbes.ru's account that Media3's subsidiary Delovoy Mir Onlayn acquired Cian in July 2013 and leadership passed to Melnikov about six months later, independently corroborated by CNews stating he led Cian since 2014) reconciles both accounts: 2013 = the Media3/Delovoy Mir Onlayn acquisition of Cian / Melnikov's arrival at the group, 2014 = his formal CEO title. The JSON's existing 2014 start_year is kept (SEC-filed, legally-disclosed, most authoritative), now with a documented, evidence-based reconciliation instead of a silent pick between conflicting sources.

3) GICS gap follow-up: Media3 Holding's business (previously null for lack of any source) was re-investigated. Forbes.ru shows its Delovoy Mir Onlayn subsidiary ran online real-estate/auto/jobs classifieds (the same GICS bucket as Cian itself), while separate lower-tier aggregator sources (mainfin.ru; a wiki.fa100.ru-sourced summary reproduced by izbran.com) describe it as also owning print/broadcast media titles. Because the holding's own operating businesses genuinely span two different GICS buckets and the print-media claim could not be verified against a higher-tier source (wiki.fa100.ru was unreachable in three attempts), sector/industry_group/industry remain null -- now a reasoned, evidenced null rather than a bare gap.

4) GICS label sanity-check (task 2): every professional_experience entry with a non-null GICS triple for both people (Cian / MKPAO Cian roles, FL.ru, HeadHunter Group PLC) was checked against the organization's real primary business; all were already exact-row matches consistent with gics_taxonomy.json and the organization's actual business (online real-estate classifieds; freelance labor marketplace; online recruitment marketplace respectively). No mislabeled GICS triple was found for this ticker; nothing was changed under this check.

5) HONEST-GAP FOLLOW-UP attempts (bounded, one per gap): (a) Grigoriev's FL.ru end year -- 2 fresh WebSearch queries plus WebFetch of 3 new URLs not tried in prior rounds (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dmitry_Grigoryev_(businessman) -- a same-named Kazakh businessman, b. 1975, unrelated, rejected as a new namesake; ir.ciangroup.ru/en/corporate-governance/management/dmitry-grigoriev/ -- 404; interfax.ru/business/837738 -- repeats the already-known 3-line summary). Still unresolved, remains null. (b) Melnikov's exact graduation years for both credentials -- 2 fresh WebSearch queries plus WebFetch of mainfin.ru and izbran.com (citing wiki.fa100.ru) surfaced candidate years (1999 Finance Academy, 2006 Stanford MBA) but a direct re-fetch of mainfin.ru's own text did not contain these years, and wiki.fa100.ru itself could not be reached (connection refused, 3 attempts) to verify independently; the candidate years do not meet the confirmation bar and were NOT added. Still unresolved, remains null. (c) Melnikov's pre-Media3 employers -- the same mainfin.ru/izbran.com sources named Sistema Telecom, investment bank Olma, Strategic Investment Group and MDC Partners for the 1996-2004 period, but the two accounts disagree on specific sub-dates and neither could be cross-checked against a primary/high-tier source within this round's bounded budget; NOT added as a new professional_experience entry. Still unresolved, remains null -- now logged with named leads for a future round instead of a blind re-search.

6) No previously confirmed fact was deleted or overwritten in this round; all changes were either restorations of previously-established round-2 work that had been silently reverted, additive source citations/description enrichments backed by newly found sources, or documentation of gap-attempts that found nothing conclusive.

QUALITY PASS ROUND 2 (2026-07-30, see research_notes/CIAN/quality_pass_round2_20260730.md for full detail):

1) DESYNC CHECK: re-read every research_notes/CIAN/*.md file (rounds 1-4 for both people plus quality_pass_round1_20260729.md) against the current output/CIAN_person_info.json. No further desync or regression had occurred since round 1 -- the institution-string normalizations, the fl.ru/about and ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/HeadHunter source restorations, and the full notes/validation_notes documentation trail from round 1 were all still intact and matched exactly. Programmatic re-check confirmed both qualification_degree values remain within the ten-value enum and all three institution strings remain exact canonical keys in university_names.json.

2) GICS LABEL CORRECTNESS: every non-null sector/industry_group/industry triple (Cian/МКПАО "Циан" x7 entries, FL.ru, HeadHunter Group PLC) was independently re-checked programmatically against gics_taxonomy.json for exact-row validity and against each organization's real primary business. All confirmed correct; no mislabeling found; nothing changed under this check.

3) HONEST-GAP FOLLOW-UP (bounded, one attempt per remaining gap): this session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted before any of this round's planned fresh queries could be issued (a session-wide constraint, consistent with what rounds 3 and 4 separately documented), so all follow-up this round used WebFetch/direct HTML retrieval instead. (a) Grigoriev's FL.ru end year -- fetched Cian's first Grigoriev-era SEC annual filing (Form 20-F for FY2022, filed 27 April 2023) directly as HTML for the first time (prior rounds only reached the unparseable cloudfront PDF of this filing family); it independently confirms the existing bio facts but still gives only 'for 6 years' with no specific end year. Still unresolved. (b) Melnikov's exact graduation years -- tadviser.ru's URL pattern for a dedicated person page 404s (no such page); rbc.ru's tag page 403s; the newly-fetched SEC F-1 (13 October 2021) and 20-F (27 April 2023) both state the two credentials with no graduation year for either. Still unresolved. (c) Melnikov's pre-Media3 employers -- the same two newly-fetched SEC filings name no employer before Media3 Holding. Still unresolved. (d) Media3 Holding's GICS classification (previously an informed null) -- RESOLVED this round. The HTML text of Cian's SEC F-1 and 20-F, fetched directly for the first time, states verbatim that Media3 Holding was 'a large print and digital media holding company focused on selling print media businesses and investing in online media ventures'; this was independently corroborated by directly verifying (not just summarizing) ru.wikipedia.org's article on ЗАО «Медиа3», which names Maxim Melnikov as its General Director and describes the same diversified print-plus-digital media conglomerate (largest Moscow printing facility, ~2,600-point print retail network, the newspapers Труд/Экстра-М/Аргументы и факты, several internet portals), classifying its own industry as 'Медиа' (Media) in its infobox. sector/industry_group/industry for the Media3 Holding professional_experience entry are now set to Communication Services / Media & Entertainment / Media (an exact gics_taxonomy.json row), replacing round 1's reasoned null with a sourced, confirmed value.

4) No previously confirmed fact was deleted or overwritten this round; the Media3 GICS change replaces a documented null with a newly-sourced value (not a value-vs-value conflict), and all other changes are additive source citations and description/notes enrichment.
